title: 3rd Stopping Place 3rd Truth Applying The Spring Army And The Travelers Judgment On Resurrection

questions.question: After reading about spring, what strong conclusion did the traveler make about people who deny coming back to life after death?
questions.answer: He concluded that punishment in Hell would be fair for them.

questions.question: Why did he think that punishment would be fair?
questions.answer: Because denying resurrection means rejecting many promises and denying Allah’s power.

questions.question: Whose promises are being rejected when a person denies resurrection?
questions.answer: The promises given through all of Allah’s prophets.

questions.question: How often does the passage say this promise was given through the prophets?
questions.answer: Many times, even thousands of times.

questions.question: Besides the prophets, what other source clearly teaches resurrection in the passage?
questions.answer: The Qur’an teaches it in many verses.

questions.question: According to the passage, is resurrection hard or easy for Allah compared with what happens every spring?
questions.answer: It is easier for Allah than the many amazing gatherings seen in spring.

questions.question: What example from nature is used to help people understand resurrection?
questions.answer: The many living things being brought together again in spring.

questions.question: What mistake is made by someone who denies resurrection?
questions.answer: That person refuses to believe Allah’s promise and power.

questions.question: Who answered the traveler at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: His own lower self, or nafs, answered him.

questions.question: What was the reply of his nafs?
questions.answer: It said that it believed what he had said.

questions.question: What belief is the main topic of the traveler’s words?
questions.answer: Belief in resurrection and the final gathering.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does denying resurrection say about a person’s view of Allah?
questions.answer: It shows that the person is denying Allah’s power and truthfulness in His promise.

questions.question: Why is denying resurrection not a small mistake in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it goes against many clear messages sent by Allah.

questions.question: Through whom did Allah repeatedly announce resurrection?
questions.answer: Through all of His prophets.

questions.question: How else did Allah announce resurrection besides sending prophets?
questions.answer: He made it known in many verses of the Qur’an, both clearly and indirectly.

questions.question: What comparison does the traveler make between resurrection and springtime events?
questions.answer: He says resurrection is easier than the amazing renewals that happen every spring.

questions.question: What does this comparison teach about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah’s power is unlimited and fully able to raise the dead.

questions.question: What feeling does the traveler’s statement show about Allah’s judgment?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah’s judgment is just, not unfair.

questions.question: How do we know the traveler’s inner struggle moves toward faith by the end?
questions.answer: Because his nafs ends by agreeing and believing.

questions.question: What is one main lesson from this passage?
questions.answer: We should believe in resurrection because Allah has promised it and shown signs of it.

questions.question: In this passage, what did the traveler say is deserved by those who reject resurrection?
questions.answer: He said they deserve the punishment of Hell.

questions.question: What reason does he give first for that judgment?
questions.answer: He says they are turning away from many promises.

questions.question: What reason does he give next about Allah?
questions.answer: He says they are denying Allah’s complete power.

questions.question: What do the prophets have to do with this message?
questions.answer: They were told again and again to give the message that resurrection will happen.

questions.question: Does the passage present resurrection as a doubtful teaching or a strongly confirmed one?
questions.answer: It presents it as strongly confirmed.

questions.question: What two ways does the passage say the Qur’an points to resurrection?
questions.answer: By direct statements and by hints.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention spring so much?
questions.answer: Because spring is a clear sign that Allah can bring life again.

questions.question: What can a student infer about Allah’s ability from this comparison?
questions.answer: If Allah does the amazing things of spring again and again, then raising people again is surely within His power.

questions.question: Why is the nafs answering important in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows the traveler’s inner self accepts the truth after thinking about it.

questions.question: What is the final response of the nafs in simple words?
questions.answer: It says, “We believe.”

questions.question: What subject was the traveler thinking about after looking at the signs of one spring?
questions.answer: He was thinking about resurrection and the fairness of judgment.

questions.question: What punishment does he connect with denying resurrection?
questions.answer: He connects it with Hell.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is this punishment called fair?
questions.answer: Because the denial opposes clear promises and rejects Allah’s power.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s promise of resurrection?
questions.answer: It teaches that the promise was repeated many times and is certain.

questions.question: Who received and shared these promises with people?
questions.answer: The prophets did.

questions.question: What book is named as another proof for resurrection?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Does the passage say the Qur’an mentions resurrection in only one way?
questions.answer: No. It says the Qur’an mentions it in more than one way.

questions.question: What are those two ways?
questions.answer: It mentions it openly and also through hints.

questions.question: How is the final resurrection compared to spring in difficulty?
questions.answer: The final resurrection is said to be easier for Allah than the many renewals of spring.

questions.question: What does this tell us about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: His power has no limit and is not made weak by big tasks.

questions.question: At the end of the passage, what change happens inside the traveler?
questions.answer: His inner self stops resisting and accepts the truth.

questions.question: What is a good faith lesson a Muslim student can take from this passage?
questions.answer: We should trust Allah’s promise about the Hereafter and learn from the signs He shows in creation.

questions.question: What did the traveler decide about people who deny being raised after death?
questions.answer: He decided that punishment for them would be deserved.

questions.question: Which place of punishment is mentioned?
questions.answer: Hell is mentioned.

questions.question: What does denial of resurrection mean about Allah’s promises?
questions.answer: It means treating His promises as false.

questions.question: What does denial of resurrection mean about Allah’s ability?
questions.answer: It means refusing to accept His power.

questions.question: How strongly had the message of resurrection been delivered, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It had been delivered over and over again in a very strong way.

questions.question: Who delivered this message to people?
questions.answer: Allah’s prophets delivered it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an’s teaching on this matter?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an teaches resurrection in many verses.

questions.question: Why does the traveler mention the amazing events of spring?
questions.answer: To show an example of Allah bringing life and gathering things in a wonderful way.

questions.question: What is the relationship between spring and the final resurrection in the passage?
questions.answer: Spring is a smaller sign that helps people understand the greater resurrection.

questions.question: Who speaks back to the traveler after his reflection?
questions.answer: His nafs speaks back.

questions.question: How does the passage end: with rejection, doubt, or belief?
questions.answer: It ends with belief.

questions.question: What was the traveler’s first big statement after thinking about one spring?
questions.answer: He said that Hell’s punishment is just for those who deny resurrection.

questions.question: What belief are those people rejecting?
questions.answer: They are rejecting that Allah will raise people again and gather them.

questions.question: Why is rejecting that belief such a serious wrong in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it denies what Allah promised many times.

questions.question: Who are mentioned as witnesses to those promises?
questions.answer: All of the prophets are mentioned.

questions.question: What other source supports the promise besides the prophets?
questions.answer: Many verses of the Qur’an support it.

questions.question: According to the passage, how certain is the promise of resurrection?
questions.answer: It is very certain and strongly confirmed.

questions.question: What natural event is used as a sign of this truth?
questions.answer: The repeated reviving and gathering seen in spring.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the final resurrection with these spring events?
questions.answer: It says the final resurrection is even easier for Allah.

questions.question: What quality of Allah is especially highlighted by this comparison?
questions.answer: His unlimited power is highlighted.

questions.question: What does the traveler seem to be doing by speaking to himself?
questions.answer: He is reminding his own soul with proofs and trying to strengthen faith.

questions.question: What response does his nafs give?
questions.answer: It accepts his words and says it believes.

questions.question: What does the ending teach about thinking carefully about Allah’s signs?
questions.answer: Careful thinking can lead the heart and soul to stronger belief.
